strings.title: Whole Numbers Times Fractions
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: To multiply a whole number by a fraction, find one part first (divide by the denominator), then take as many parts as the numerator says.
strings.keywords: of, unit fraction, one part, numerator, denominator, bar model
watchFor: Multiplying the whole number by the denominator (12 × 3/4 = 48/4 and stopping): ask "Is 3/4 of 12 more or less than 12?"
Dividing by the numerator instead of the denominator: ask "How many equal parts is the bar split into?"
Thinking the answer should be bigger than the whole number: ask "What is 1/2 of 20?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did 1/4 of 20 help with 3/4 of 20?" Land: find one part by dividing by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 12 × 3/4 and 3/4 of 12 are the same.

problems.notes: Look for: 20 split into 4 equal parts. Ask: "How big is one part?" Word choice: "one fourth of". Model: bar 1/4 of 20

responses.say: Half of 20 is 10, half of that is 5.

problems.notes: Look for: three of those parts. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: bar 3/4 of 20

responses.say: One fourth is 5, so three fourths is 15.

responses.tip: Ask: is three quarters of 20 more or less than 20?

problems.notes: Look for: one fifth is 6, two fifths is 12. Ask: "What's one part?" Model: bar 2/5 of 30

responses.say: A fifth of 30 is 6, two fifths is 12.

responses.tip: Divided by the numerator. Ask: how many equal parts does the bar have?

problems.notes: Look for: the same as 3/4 of 12. Ask: "Is 12 × 3/4 the same as 3/4 of 12?" Model: bar 3/4 of 12

responses.say: 3/4 of 12: one fourth is 3, three fourths is 9.
responses.tip: Ask: why can we switch it to 3/4 of 12?
Multiply first, then divide. Same answer.
Forgot the fourths. Ask: should 12 × 3/4 be bigger than 12?

problems.notes: Look for: a third of 15 is 5, two thirds is 10. Ask: "Which is easier: divide first, or multiply first?" Model: bar 2/3 of 15

responses.say: A third of 15 is 5, two thirds is 10.

problems.notes: Look for: an eighth of 24 is 3, five eighths is 15. Ask: "What's one eighth?" Model: bar 5/8 of 24

responses.say: An eighth of 24 is 3, so 5 eighths is 15.
Half of 24 is 12, plus one more eighth (3) is 15.
responses.tip: 5/8 as a half and an eighth.
Divided by the numerator. Ask: what does the 8 tell us?

problems.notes: Look for: an eighth of 40 is 5, three eighths is 15. Ask: "What do you notice about the last two answers?" Model: bar 3/8 of 40

responses.say: An eighth of 40 is 5, three eighths is 15.
